name: Question 11
problem: What is the curvature of the curve $r(t)=⟨3t,1-{t}^{3}⟩$, for $t>0?$
worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{3})⟩=⟨3,-3{t}^{2}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-3{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =3\sqrt{1+{t}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})⟩=⟨0,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨3,\,-3{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-6t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & -3{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -6t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}3 & -3{t}^{2} \\ 0 & -6t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-18t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=|-18t|=18t.
$$

Notice that since $t>0$, we have $|t|=t.$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{18t}{(3\sqrt{1+{t}^{4}})^{3}} \\  & =\frac{18t}{27(1+{t}^{4})^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{3(1+{t}^{4})^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

What is the curvature of the curve r(t)=⟨3t,1−t3⟩, for t>0?

a
6t1+t4
b
t27(1+t4)3/2
c
131+t4
d
t9(1+t4)3/2
e
2t3(1+t4)3/2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curvature κ is given by κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t) and ‖r′(t)‖:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(3t),ddt(1−t3)⟩=⟨3,−3t2⟩‖r′(t)‖=32+(−3t2)2=9+9t4=31+t4

Now, we find the second derivative:

r″(t)=⟨ddt(3),ddt(−3t2)⟩=⟨0,−6t⟩

Next, we compute the cross product by considering r′(t) and r″(t) as 3-dimensional vectors with zero z-components:

r′(t)×r″(t)=⟨3,−3t2,0⟩×⟨0,−6t,0⟩=ijk3−3t200−6t0=3−3t20−6tk=−18tk

So, the magnitude of the cross product is ‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖=|−18t|=18t. Notice that since t>0, we have |t|=t.

Therefore, the curvature is

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3=18t(31+t4)3=18t27(1+t4)3/2=2t3(1+t4)3/2.
